title: Rust test record sheet
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Metals and their uses (8G); energy transfers (8K)
source: Written for science/y8 lesson 44 (Rust test record sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 44: Corrosion and rusting. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Corrosion
points: Metals react with air, water, acids

model.title: Write the word equation for rusting.

parts.text: iron + oxygen + water → hydrated iron oxide

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: iron + oxygen + water → hydrated iron oxide (rust)

panels.title: Our fair test (at home)
points: Jar A: nail in tap water (air and water)
Jar B: nail in salty water
Jar C: nail in a dry jar with dry rice (little water)

panels.title: Safety guide: the rust test
points: Use clean steel nails; handle carefully, points down
Jars with lids, labelled, out of reach of young children
Do not touch the salt water then your eyes
Wash hands after; an adult disposes of nails

keywords.def: a metal slowly reacting with substances around it
hydrated iron oxide formed when iron corrodes
a reaction in which a substance gains oxygen
a dull layer formed on a metal surface
what is present, such as air or water

questions.q: A bike left outside in winter rusts faster near salted roads. Explain.
questions.a: It has water and oxygen, and salt speeds up rusting

questions.q: Why does a stainless steel spoon not rust in the dishwasher?
questions.a: It is an alloy made to resist corrosion

questions.q: Is rusting a physical or chemical change?
Core: Set up the three-jar rust test with an adult. Write the variables and a prediction, and draw day 0.
questions.a: Variables: change conditions, observe rust, control nail type and jar; prediction with reason

questions.q: Extend: Why must the nails be the same size and type?
questions.a: So only the conditions change, to keep the test fair

questions.q: Stretch: How could you make a jar with water but almost no oxygen? (adult method)
questions.a: Boil water to remove air, cool, add the nail and a layer of oil on top
C) Nail in a dry jar. Without water, iron cannot rust.

questions.q: Big question: why does the anchor rust but the drawer nail does not?
questions.a: The anchor has water and oxygen (and salt); the drawer is dry.
